subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: When the axes are rotated through an angle α, find the transformed equation of xcosα + ysinα = p.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what happens to the two Y terms, and which identity finishes it.

steps.label: Take the given equation
steps.margin_note: First mark. This one carries no numbers at all — the angle of rotation is the SAME α that appears in the equation, which is what makes the answer come out so short.

recall.must_convey: That the given equation is the original one, and its angle α is also the angle of rotation.
accept: the given equation is the original one and alpha is the rotation angle
take x cos alpha plus y sin alpha equals p as the original
the angle in the equation is the same as the angle of rotation
ichchina equation original, alpha ye rotation angle
write the given equation and number it

steps.why: The first move is to label which equation you were handed. A transformation question is always one of two shapes — given the original find the new, or given the new find the original — and every later step depends on which.
common_mistakes: Introducing a second letter for the rotation angle when it is the same α.
Reading p as a variable rather than a constant.

steps.label: Write the change of axes
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The standard rotation formulas with θ = α. Nothing is evaluated, because α stays a letter throughout.
lines: Angle of rotation θ = α, then
x = Xcosθ − Ysinθ  ⇒  x = Xcosα − Ysinα
y = Ycosθ + Xsinθ  ⇒  y = Ycosα + Xsinα

recall.must_convey: That the rotation formulas are written with θ = α.
accept: x equals X cos alpha minus Y sin alpha and y equals Y cos alpha plus X sin alpha
write the rotation formulas with theta equal to alpha
put theta equals alpha in the standard formulas
theta place lo alpha pettali
the rotation formulas with alpha

steps.why: Under a rotation through θ the old coordinates are mixtures of both new ones: x = Xcosθ − Ysinθ and y = Ycosθ + Xsinθ. Writing them down correctly is most of the work.
common_mistakes: Putting a number in for α when it must stay general.
Getting the sign of the sine term wrong in x.

steps.label: Substitute into the equation
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Substituting gives four terms; group the ones carrying X and the ones carrying Y before doing anything else.
lines: ⇒ Xcos²α − Ysinα cosα + Ycosα sinα + Xsin²α = p

recall.must_convey: That substituting gives Xcos²α − Ysinαcosα + Ycosαsinα + Xsin²α = p.
accept: substitute both expressions and expand the two brackets
put the rotation formulas into the given equation
multiply out cos alpha and sin alpha across the brackets
rendu brackets ni expand cheyyali
substitute into the given equation

steps.why: Substitution is mechanical once the formulas are down. Every x and every y in the given equation is replaced, including the ones inside a squared bracket.
common_mistakes: Multiplying only the first term of each bracket.
Losing one of the two mixed terms before they can cancel.

steps.label: Simplify to the answer
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The two Y terms are equal and opposite, so they cancel outright; the two X terms carry cos²α + sin²α, which is 1. What is left is a single letter.
lines: ⇒ X(cos²α + sin²α) = p      [∵ the two Y terms cancel]

recall.must_convey: That the Y terms cancel and cos²α + sin²α = 1, leaving X = p.
accept: the Y terms cancel and cos squared plus sin squared is one so X equals p
the two Y terms are equal and opposite so they cancel
using the identity the answer is X equals p
Y terms cancel avuthaayi, cos square plus sin square one
the transformed equation is X equals p

steps.why: Rotating the axes through the line's own normal angle turns it into a line perpendicular to the new X-axis at distance p — which is exactly what X = p says.
common_mistakes: Cancelling the X terms instead of the Y terms.
Leaving the answer as X(cos²α + sin²α) = p without using the identity.
